The problem

Today, an AI agent can present itself as authorized to make a purchase — but the payment system has no reliable way to check. API keys don't prove identity, don't enforce limits, and don't expire.

No identity verification

A stolen API key looks identical to a legitimate one. The system can't tell who's really calling.

No scope enforcement

A grocery bot with full API access can buy anything — there's no way to limit spend or category.

No instant revocation

If an agent goes rogue, you can't shut it down in real time. Key rotation is slow and breaks other integrations.

How KYA works

Four steps — from issuing a scoped permission slip to revoking it instantly.

01

Issue

Create a scoped, signed, short-lived credential for each agent — with explicit spend limits, allowed categories, and expiry.

02

Verify

Every agent transaction is checked against the credential in real time — amount, category, expiry, revocation status — before any money moves.

03

Monitor

Behavioural anomaly detection watches for unusual patterns — late-night spikes, spend ceiling approaches, frequency anomalies — and flags them for review.

04

Revoke

Instantly kill an agent's authority. Every future request is denied immediately, with a full audit trail of who revoked and why.

Built for fintech-grade security

Cryptographic credentials

Every credential is a signed JWT encoding the agent's exact scope. No shared secrets, no API keys that never expire.

Real-time verification

Sub-12ms verification checks signature, revocation, expiry, amount, and category in a single synchronous hot path.

Immutable audit trail

Every decision, every revocation, every policy change — logged permanently with actor, rationale, and timestamp.

Fail-safe by default

Choose between fail-safe (block all) and fail-open (allow all) during outages. Configurable per your risk appetite.

Role-based access

Senior admins can configure policy. Analysts can review and resolve flags. Everyone sees what they need, nothing more.

Developer-first APIs

RESTful endpoints with code samples in multiple languages. Issue, verify, and revoke credentials programmatically.
